source_conversation.content: I'm on Windows 11 and I want to get rid of the Spotify app because I don't use it anymore. Can you walk me through it?

sections.text: On Windows 11: Open Start, go to 'All apps,' and search the list for the app. Press and hold the app, or right-click it, then choose 'Uninstall.' Open Start, then Settings, then Apps, then 'Installed apps.' Find the app, select 'More,' then choose 'Uninstall.' Some apps can't be uninstalled from the Settings app right now. For these, use the Control Panel method in the 'Uninstall from Control Panel' section. Apps built into Windows can't be uninstalled, so you may not see an Uninstall option for them.

On Mac: Quit the app first. If the app is currently open, quit the app before continuing. Locate it in the Applications folder, or use Spotlight with Command (⌘) and double-click. If the app isn't made by Apple, find out whether it includes an 'Uninstall' or 'Uninstaller' app. If the app doesn't include an uninstall app or feature, drag the app to the Trash. If you're asked for a user name and password, enter the name and password of an administrator account on your Mac. To permanently delete the app and make its storage space available for other items, choose Finder > Empty Trash. You can't use the Finder to delete apps that are required by your Mac. If you can't delete an app because your Mac says that it's in use, make sure that the app isn't open.

sections.text: On iPhone: On your iPhone or iPad, open the App Store. Browse the Today, Games, Apps, or Arcade tabs, or tap the Search tab to look for a specific app. Tap the price or Get button. If you see the Open button instead, you already bought or downloaded the app. You might need to enter your Apple Account password to complete the download. Confirm the purchase by double-clicking the side button on your iPhone. With Face ID, glance at the device. With Touch ID, rest your finger on the button. An app with a Get button instead of a price is free, and you won't be charged to download it. Free apps may offer in-app purchases and subscriptions.

On Android: Open Google Play. On a phone or tablet, use the Play Store app. Find the app you want. Check the app's reliability. Under the app's title, look at its star ratings and number of downloads. To read individual reviews, scroll to the 'Ratings and reviews' section. When you choose an app, tap 'Install' for free apps, or tap the app's price for paid apps. Some of these steps work only on Android 8.0 and up.
